summary:
Public Law 118-229, the "Fishery Improvement to Streamline untimely regulatory Hurdles post Emergency Situation Act" or "FISHES Act" (H.R. 5103, approved January 4, 2025), amends the fishery resource disaster assistance provisions of the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act to impose statutory deadlines on the processing of "spend plans" submitted by disaster-relief requesters and to constrain the review role of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB).

Section 2 amends Section 312(a)(6) of the Magnuson-Stevens Act (16 U.S.C. 1861a(a)(6)) in two respects.

First, paragraph (1) rewrites subparagraph (D) ("Spend plans"). New clause (i) conditions receipt of an allocation from funds available under paragraph (9) on a requester with an affirmative fishery resource disaster determination submitting a spend plan to the Secretary not later than 120 days after notification that funds are available. The plan must include, as applicable: (I) objectives and outcomes emphasizing the factors contributing to the disaster and the minimization of future uninsured losses; (II) a statement of work; and (III) budget details. New clause (ii) establishes a review mechanism: under subclause (I), the Secretary must review the plan for completeness and provide notice within 10 days; under subclause (II), if the Secretary determines a plan is incomplete, the completeness notice must include a detailed description of the information needed for the plan to be deemed complete.

Second, paragraph (2) rewrites subparagraph (F)(i) ("Availability"). New subclause (I) requires that funds be made available to grantees not later than 90 days after the Secretary receives a complete spend plan. New subclause (II) permits the Director of OMB, if so requested, to review a completed spend plan concurrently with the Secretary, but expressly bars the Director from delaying the 90-day timeline in subclause (I).

The Act contains no appropriation; it operates on funds otherwise made available under paragraph (9) of Section 312(a)(6) and does not authorize new spending. The measure prescribes procedural deadlines (10-day completeness review; 120-day submission window; 90-day disbursement requirement) but includes no separate general effective-date provision, taking effect upon enactment. The short title provisions are codified as a note to 16 U.S.C. 1801.

Notwithstanding the enacting title's reference to the Director of OMB approving or denying spend plans within a specified time, the operative text vests completeness review in the Secretary and limits OMB to a concurrent, non-delaying review of completed plans.
